title: Traffic Relay Runbook and Anchor Log
body:
Purpose:
This is my personal runbook for orchestrating a staged traffic relay (small cohorts -> ramp -> steady) for model flips and capacity-sensitive releases. It focuses on stepwise traffic shifts using anchors, relay lanes, and temporary client quarantines. Use it as a quick reference on release day; not exhaustive.

Summary / when to use:
- Minor model swaps or config flips where we expect small user-impact risk (metric regressions, hallucination changes).
- Capacity-constrained deploys where we need tight control over per-tenant throughput.
- Any release that requires reversible routing (no DB migrations).

High-level strategy:
1) Reserve two relay lanes in the routing fabric: stable-anchor (existing model) and candidate-lane (new model).
2) Seed candidate-lane with very low traffic (0.5%–2% depending on size).
3) Observe targeted signals for 45–90m windows.
4) If green, step traffic in multiplicative increments (2x–3x) following the ramp table below.
5) If any 'stop' criteria hit, immediately reroute candidate traffic back to stable-anchor and create an incident note.

Preflight checklist (T-48h -> T-1h):
- [ ] Confirm model artifact hash and canonical alias (model:vX) in model registry. (linked PR above)
- [ ] Confirm routing policy stub exists in routing-config (route-id: relay/2024-11-priyanka).
- [ ] Reservation: allocate candidate-lane in dedicated pool or tag nodes for soft isolation.
- [ ] Telemetry: ensure dashboards for the following are live and pinned: request_latency_p95, token_cost_per_1000, error_rate_5m, user_drop_rate, hallucination-rate (if eval hooks exist).
- [ ] Alerts: temp lower thresholds for this release window: latency_p95 >= 600ms (page), error_rate >= 0.8% (page), user_drop_rate >= 1% (sev2).
- [ ] Canary cohort list: create small list of client IDs / tenants to include in initial 0.5% cohort (prefer low-volume tenants).
- [ ] Slack channel: #launch-relay-2024-11 and add SRE, infra oncall, product-eng, and CS liaisons.
- [ ] Dry-run: execute the routing change in staging and run through rollback steps.

Ramp table (suggested):
- Step 0: 0% -> 0.5% (seed) — 45m observation
- Step 1: 0.5% -> 1.5% — 60m observation
- Step 2: 1.5% -> 4% — 90m observation
- Step 3: 4% -> 12% — 60m observation
- Step 4: 12% -> 30% — 30m observation
- Step 5: 30% -> 60% — 15m observation
- Full: 60% -> 100% only if all signals look stable AND infra capacity tested

Commands / operator quick hits:
- Apply routing weight (kubernetes/edge route API example):
  curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/v1/routes/relay/2024-11-priyanka/weights 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_KEY" 
    -d '{"stable-anchor": 70, "candidate-lane": 30}'
  (replace with internal sdk: routing.set_weights(route, {stable:70, candidate:30}))

- One-off: isolate tenant to stable-anchor (immediate escape hatch):
  routing.pin_tenant(tenant_id, "stable-anchor") // SDK pseudocode

Telemetry queries (Prometheus / metrics):
- p95 latency scoped to candidate-lane: sum(histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{lane="candidate-lane"}[5m])) )
- error rate: sum(rate(requests_total{lane="candidate-lane", code=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total{lane="candidate-lane"}[5m]))
- user impact: rate(user_drop_total{lane="candidate-lane"}[5m])
- cost: token_cost_total{lane="candidate-lane"} / requests_total{lane="candidate-lane"}

Stop / rollback criteria (immediate):
- page if: p95 latency >= 900ms sustained for 5m OR error rate >= 2% sustained for 5m.
- rollback if: any of the above OR clear degradation in QA eval hooks (regression delta > 6% on key prompts).
- manual rollback: set candidate-lane weight to 0 and confirm all in-flight requests drained (~30s).

Post-rollback notes to capture:
- timestamp, last-applied-weight, immediate metric diffs, affected-tenants list, incident slack thread link, remediation steps attempted.

Post-success checklist (after reaching target fraction and holding for 24h):
- [ ] Promote model alias to stable (model:current -> model:vX).
- [ ] Remove candidate-lane reservation and free tags.
- [ ] Revert temporary alert thresholds to baseline.
- [ ] Create annotated release note (link to PR and perf traces) and CC CS for customer communication if any tenants were in early cohorts.

Operational nuances / gotchas (things I forget):
- Small tenants: they can skew signal if one tenant has bursty behavior. Use cohort selection to avoid attribution noise.
- KV cache warmness: candidate lane may be cold; expect initial latency spike. Factor that into p95 expectations for first 30m.
- SDK toggles: if customers use client-side model aliasing, coordinate with client SDK team to avoid double-routing.
- Backpressure: if downstream queues fill, we need to throttle candidate-lane at the ingress (rate limiter) — do not shift more traffic until queue drains.

Communication cadence (on release day):
- +0m: announce seed start in #launch-relay-2024-11 with weights snapshot.
- +15m: quick check (p95 & error) — thumbs up/downs.
- Every observation window end: post metric deltas and decision (advance / hold / rollback).
- On any page: ping SRE oncall, mention incident link, and call for triage.

Example short incident log (template for slack and incident doc):
- time: 2024-11-22T09:13Z
- action: ramped to 4%
- observation: p95 candidate-lane jumped from 340ms -> 760ms within 6m
- decision: rollback to 0% at 09:19Z
- remediation: increased pool size and bumped routing kernel; re-run at 10:40Z

Open questions / TODOs (followups):
- [ ] Instrument per-prompt quality hooks for the handful of high-signal prompts before next release (see eval harness ticket REDW-2011).
- [ ] Short circuit for "tenant quarantine" that can be applied by CS without engineering intervention (self-serve pinning UI idea).
- [ ] Capture a lightweight synthetic load script that mimics our top-20 tenants for better stage tests.

Notes to self:
- Keep the initial seeding conservative for large global launches; the noise floor increases with total RPS.
- When in doubt, prefer slower ramp. The cost of re-run is less than customer trust erosion.
- Link back to this doc from any release PR to reduce tribal knowledge.

References:
- routing-config repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-config/pull/122
- dry-run checklist in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=deploy-anchors
- follow-up eval ticket: https://linear.app/REDW/issue/2011/eval-harness-add-high-signal-prompts

End of runbook (WIP).
